[[Image:Thue-number.svg|thumb|The Thue number of the 5-[[Cycle graph|cycle]] is four.]]
In the [[Mathematics|mathematical]] area of [[graph theory]], the '''Thue number''' of a graph is a variation of the [[chromatic index]], defined by {{harvtxt|Alon|Grytczuk|Hałuszczak|Riordan|2002}} and named after mathematician [[Axel Thue]], who studied the [[squarefree word]]s used to define this number.

Alon et al. define a ''nonrepetitive coloring'' of a graph to be an assignment of colors to the edges of the graph, such that there does not exist any even-length [[path (graph theory)|simple path]] in the graph in which the colors of the edges in the first half of the path form the same sequence as the colors of the edges in the second half of the path. The Thue number of a graph is the minimum number of colors needed in any nonrepetitive coloring.{{sfnp|Alon|Grytczuk|Hałuszczak|Riordan|2002}}

Variations on this concept involving vertex colorings or more general walks on a graph have been studied by several authors.<ref>{{harvtxt|Barát|Varjú|2008}}; {{harvtxt|Barát|Wood|2005}}; {{harvtxt|Brešar|Klavžar|2004}}; {{harvtxt|Kündgen|Pelsmajer|2008}}.</ref>

== Example ==

Consider a [[pentagon]], that is, a [[Cycle graph|cycle]] <math>C_5</math> of five vertices. If its edges are colored with two colors, some two adjacent edges will have the same color <math>x</math>; the path formed by those two edges will have the repetitive color sequence <math>xx</math>.  If its edges are colored with three colors, one of the three colors will be used only once; the path of four edges formed by the other two colors will either have two consecutive edges or will form the repetitive color sequence <math>xyxy</math>.  However, all repetitions can be avoided by using four colors, with one color repeated on two non-adjacent edges. Therefore, the Thue number of <math>C_5</math> is four.{{sfnp|Alon|Grytczuk|Hałuszczak|Riordan|2002}}

== Results ==

Alon et al. use the [[Lovász local lemma]] to prove that the Thue number of any graph is at most quadratic in its maximum degree; they provide an example showing that for some graphs this quadratic dependence is necessary.  In addition they show that the Thue number of a path of four or more vertices is exactly three, that the Thue number of any cycle is at most four, and that the Thue number of the [[Petersen graph]] is exactly five.{{sfnp|Alon|Grytczuk|Hałuszczak|Riordan|2002}}

The cycles <math>C_5</math>,  <math>C_7</math>,  <math>C_9</math>,  <math>C_{10}</math>,  <math>C_{14}</math>, and  <math>C_{17}</math> have Thue number four.{{sfnp|Alon|Grytczuk|Hałuszczak|Riordan|2002}} Resolving a conjecture of Alon et al., Currie showed that all other cycles have Thue number three.{{sfnp|Currie|2002}}

== Computational complexity ==

Testing whether a coloring has a repetitive path is in NP, so testing whether a coloring is nonrepetitive is in [[co-NP]], and Manin showed that it is [[co-NP-complete]]. The problem of finding such a coloring belongs to <math>\Sigma_2^P</math> in the [[polynomial hierarchy]], and again Manin showed that it is complete for this level.{{sfnp|Manin|2007}}
